meetings.title: 14th Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: The agenda of today's meeting was to discuss and take a decision on the letters received by the committee. In this regard, the first item on the agenda was to take a decision on the letter sent by the Maldives Media Council. As the Maldives Media Council Act amendment bill has not yet been introduced to the Parliament, the committee decided that the committee will meet with the relevant parties regarding such an amendment bill once the committee starts the process of reviewing the bill. Hence, Thulusdhoo Constituency Member Ibrahim Naseem proposed to inform the Maldives Medial Council, that the council shall discuss with the Attorney General's Office the inclusion of amendments to the Maldives Media Council Act amendment bill during the drafting process of the bill, and to ask the council to share the amendments with the Attorney General’s Office in this regard. This proposal was seconded by Henveiru West Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim. The voting details are as follows. Vote : To inform the Maldives Medial Council, that the council shall discuss with the Attorney General's Office the inclusion of amendments to Maldives Media Council Act amendment bill during the drafting process of the bill, and to ask the council to share the amendments with the Attorney General’s Office in this regard. Total number of members: 11 Number of members present: 6 Voted Yes: 5 Voted against: 0 Abstain: 0 Total voted: 5 Required to Pass: 4 Result: Approved unanimously by the members present in the meeting. Hence, the members present in the committee unanimously voted to inform the Maldives Medial Council, that the council shall discuss with the Attorney General's Office the inclusion of amendments to Maldives Media Council Act amendment bill during the drafting process of the bill, and to ask the council to share the amendments with the Attorney General’s Office in this regard. Then the committee moved on to take a decision based on the letter sent by the National Integrity Commission. In view of the current economic situation in the Maldives, the Committee is of the view that it is not appropriate to appoint new staff to the posts mentioned in the letter, at a time when the President's Office Number: 9/2024/57/(PRA)POL-1 (3 July 2024) has directed all state institutions to reduce public expenditure. It was decided to inform the National Integrity Commission that the committee would take note of the budget concerns of the institution, while the budget for the year 2025 is being presented in the Parliament and the process is underway. Next, the committee made a decision on the letter sent by the Anti-Corruption Commission. Since the letter was sent in secrecy, the work on the letter was carried out by the committee in secrecy. It was decided that the committee would take note of the budgetary concerns of the commission, while the State Budget for the year 2025 is being present to the Parliament. Lastly, in response to an earlier letter submitted to the committee, the task of examining the attendance of the members appointed to the commissions which are under the committee's mandate was carried out. Since the committee does not find that the manner in which the attendance have been sent now is the most appropriate, the committee decided on seeking the details of the commission's members attendance between January 1, 2024 to April 30, 2024 (time to attend the commission, sign-in and sign-out time, and the details of individual members should be known separately). Additionally, if a decision has been taken in regard to how and when the commission members should be present to the commission, the committee decided to write to the commissions under the committee’s mandate, to share the policy or decision with the committee.

meetings.summary: The first item on the agenda of today's meeting was the committee's decision on how to deal with letters and copy letters sent by the general public. In this regard, Kolamaafushi Constituency Member Ibrahim Didi supported the proposal of Thulusdhoo Constituency Ibrahim Naseem to send the letter and the reply sent to the committee's official WhatsApp group. The following is a summary of how members voted for the motion. Voting details are as follows: Vote : To send the letter received from public and the reply sent to the committee's official WhatsApp group. Total number of members: 11 Number of members present: 9 Voted Yes: 8 Voted against: 0 Abstain: 0 Total voted: 8 Required to Pass: 6 Result: Approved unanimously by the members present in the meeting. Hence, the members present in the committee unanimously voted to send the letter received from public and the reply sent to the committee's official WhatsApp group. This was followed by discussions and decisions on those to be summoned for clarification while proceeding with the resolution moved by Baarashu Constituency Member Ibrahim Shujau to determine the views of the 20 th Majlis on the increasing number of members of parliament every five years. The committee decided on holding discussion meetings with the members of the Policy Section of the President's Office, members of the Special Parliament Drafting Committee, which worked on the Constitution, Political Parties and organizations, especially Transparency Maldives. Lastly, the committee met with the members of the Civil Service Commission to discuss its functioning. During the meeting, they were briefed about the problems faced by the commission in running the commission and performing its duties.

meetings.title: 2nd Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: The agenda for today’s meeting was held to discuss and decide on the work plan of the committee. Firstly, the committee discussed the working quorum and voting quorum of the committee. Member for Thulusdhoo Constituency, Ibrahim Naseem proposed to set the working quorum to 1/3 of the committee (4 members) as the Standing Order states that the working quorum of a committee shall not be lower than 1/3 of its members, and to set the voting quorum to 2/3 of the committee (6 members). Member for Henveiru Hulhangu Constituency, Ali Ibrahim seconded the proposal. The voting details are as follows. Vote: Committee Working Quorum as 4 members and Committee Voting Quorum as 6 members Total no. of members: 11 No. of members present: 10 Voted Yes: 9 Voted No: 0 Abstain: 0 Total Voted: 9 No. of votes required to Pass: 6 Vote Result: Passed with all members present and voting. Hence, the committee passed the Committee Working Quorum as 4 members and Committee Voting Quorum as 6 members, as proposed to the committee. Then the committee deliberated on the formulation of a guideline to follow regarding the issues sent to the committee, other than the issues mentioned in Article 151 (a) of the Standing Order of People’s Majlis. Therein, the committee decided on adopting the guideline in accordance with Article 151 (b) of the Standing Order. Following this, Member for Thulusdhoo Constituency, Ibrahim Naseem proposed to have introductory meetings with the institutions under the committee’s mandate. Member for Felidhoo Constituency, Adam Zahir seconded the proposal. The voting details are as follows. Vote: To hold introductory meetings with the institutions under the committee’s mandate Total no. of members: 11 No. of members present: 10 Voted Yes: 9 Voted No: 0 Abstain: 0 Total Voted: 9 No. of votes required to Pass: 6 Vote Result: Passed with all members present and voting. The committee requested the Chairperson to decide on the dates for the introductory meetings. Subsequently, the committee decided to hold the introductory meetings with the institutions under the committee’s mandate every Tuesday and Wednesday at 11:00 hours. In concluding the meeting, the committee decided to hold committee meetings every Tuesday at 11:00 hours.

meetings.title: 1st Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: This meeting was the selection of a chairperson of the committee. Legal Officer Uza. Shahzadh Saeed, conducted the process of selecting the chairman of the committee. Kolamaafushi Constituency MP Ibrahim didi proposed the name of Maafushi Constituency MP Hussain Riza Adam, this proposal was seconded by kelaa Constituency MP Abdulla Shareef. Vote: To elect Maafushi Constituency Member Hussain Riza Adam as the Chair of the Committee Total number of members : 11 Number of members present: 10 Voted Yes: 10 Voted against: 0 Abstain: 0 Required to Pass: 6 Result: Passed Hence, Maafushi Constituency Member Hussain Riza Adam was elected as the Chair of the Committee. Meanwhile, Thlusdhoo Constituency MP Ibrahim Naseem proposed the name of Kelaa Constituency MP Abdulla Shareef as deputy chair, this proposal was seconded by kolamafshi Constituency MP Ibrahim Did. With the vote of 10 members Kelaa MP Abdulla Shareef was unanimously elected as the deputy chair of the committee. Total number of members : 11 Number of members present: 10 Voted Yes: 10 Voted against: 0 Abstain: 0 Required to Pass: 6 Result: Passed Hence, Kelaa Constituency Member Abdulla Shareef was elected as the Deputy Chair of the Committee. After that Committee discussed on which days of the week committee will meet and how many days, after the discussion, committee decided that three days in a week (Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday) will meet for discussion on issues proposed to the committee.
